article.title: NFL EDGE Wednesday Evening Brief
article.dek: Detroit just entered the card at +4.5, while Washington was replaced and Arizona disappeared.

items.headline: Detroit will be missing two starting offensive linemen Thursday night
paragraphs: Detroit ruled tackle Blake Miller and guard Christian Mahogany out for Thursday night in Buffalo, while corner D.J. Reed is questionable. Buffalo lists safety Cole Bishop, running back Ty Johnson and defensive lineman T.J. Sanders as questionable; linebacker Terrel Bernard has no game designation.

items.headline: Thursday night's Buffalo weather looks much quieter than the daytime forecast
paragraphs: The National Weather Service expects showers to be most likely Thursday morning around Orchard Park, followed by partly cloudy conditions and calm wind Thursday night. At the moment, weather does not look like a reason to alter how we treat the Detroit spread recommendation.

items.headline: Washington has two Wednesday non-participants
paragraphs: Washington listed linebacker Frankie Luvu and tight end Chig Okonkwo as non-participants Wednesday. Several defenders were limited, including Dorance Armstrong, K'Lavon Chaisson, Charles Omenihu, Odafe Oweh and Daron Payne.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Detroit is now actionable, but the injury news makes price discipline even more important
paragraphs: NFL EDGE's Balanced lane has moved from Washington to Detroit +4.5. Detroit's two offensive-line absences are real information, but they are not a reason to override the governed recommendation. They are a reason to respect the exact price guardrail: the current Detroit play is +4.5 at -102 with Play Through -105.
Washington's injury report is still worth following, but Washington is no longer the current Balanced recommendation. Do not keep betting yesterday's card after the selector has moved on.

items.headline: Detroit is the interesting disagreement — but not a blind fade of Buffalo
paragraphs: The new NFL EDGE Balanced play is Detroit +4.5. Recent DraftKings reporting has Buffalo drawing roughly two-thirds of spread tickets and about nine-tenths of spread money at -4.5, so the public market is leaning hard toward the favorite. At the same time, the governed NFL EDGE card has taken the other side at the same key number.

That makes Detroit worth watching, but it does not prove the Buffalo money is wrong. I could not verify a fresh Circa split strong enough to call this a clean retail-versus-sharper-market disagreement. The useful information is simply that NFL EDGE is currently opposing heavy DraftKings concentration.
items.takeaway: If you follow the current Balanced recommendation, take Detroit +4.5 only at -105 or better. Do not chase a worse price merely because Buffalo is popular, and do not call this a full Fade signal unless a credible sharper-market comparison confirms the disagreement.

items.headline: A selector change is a new decision, not an edit to the old bet
paragraphs: When NFL EDGE replaces one team with another in a lane, treat the new recommendation as its own decision. The old team's price and Play Through do not carry forward, and neither does any emotional attachment you had to the earlier pick. Read the current side, current price and current Play Through together before betting.
